title: AI Crowds Out Fresh Grads at Wall Street Tech Hubs in India
source_used: Bloomberg, relayed by The Economic Times (Bloomberg page blocked: HTTP 403)
key_facts: Purva Jagtap, a 22-year-old engineering graduate, is applying for entry-level jobs after her family paid about $5,640 in tuition.

India's IT services sector employs about 6 million people; about 2.4 million of them work in Global Capability Centers (GCCs), which generated about $100 billion in revenue last fiscal year (NASSCOM and Zinnov-Nasscom 2026 report).
Citigroup has hired a net 2,000 people in India so far this year for its GCC operations, down from about 4,000 last year.
A McKinsey Global Institute estimate says 30% of job hours in India could be automated by 2030.
Three bankers said lower-end jobs across sales, marketing and technology are becoming redundant; JPMorgan declined to comment and Goldman Sachs did not respond.
Routine tasks such as loan processing, document checks, bookkeeping, invoicing and basic coding are increasingly being automated.
quote_evidence: Rather than widespread job losses, the impact of AI appears to be showing up through slower hiring and changing skill requirements.
Routine tasks such as loan processing, document checks, bookkeeping, invoicing and basic coding are increasingly being automated.
why_it_matters_hint: Entry-level hiring is slowing in India's bank and tech hubs while AI-skilled roles grow.
